categoryNote: Debloating category. Every entry is per-app/per-package and individually selected: an empty selection is a read-only plan, never 'all'. Store, Store Purchase App, App Installer (winget), Edge/WebView2 host, VCLibs/.NET Native/UI.Xaml/Windows App Runtime families, shell/security/compositor hosts, and the Xbox identity/Gaming Services stack are protected by default (NX12-002), and the guard is enforced inside the removal engine so no entry can bypass it. AppX and capability removals are journaled with package identity, scope and provisioned state BEFORE mutation and are honestly labeled 'Success-Irreversible' (journal replay cannot restore a package payload); restoration is the separate documented NX12-011 path. Removed inbox apps can return after Windows feature updates (documented Microsoft behavior), which is why NX12-010 keeps a ledger and every entry is idempotent. Declared cross-category conflicts: NX12-004 <-> NX13-012 (same phone-linking feature) and NX12-005 <-> NX02-008/NX11-010 (Xbox dependency cluster). No performance claims are made anywhere: app removal is a configuration change. Boundaries: NX15 owns Widgets/taskbar policy (the Widgets package is not removed here); NX11-016 owns Maps service configuration (only the Maps app is removable here); Edge and WebView2 are never removal targets.

tweaks.name: Consumer app inventory & selective removal
tweaks.description: Inventories 21 consumer AppX apps and removes only the specific ones the owner selects, per profile scope.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner drop unused consumer content apps without touching dependencies, OS components or anything that was not explicitly selected.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family Consumer (read-only inventory) and Set-NxConsumerAppState (write path) in src/nxcore/functions/NX12.ps1. The catalog is an explicit 21-name list (News, Weather, Solitaire, Clipchamp, Media Player/Movies & TV, Maps, Feedback Hub, Get Help, Tips, Office hub, Clock, Camera, Sound Recorder, Sticky Notes, Whiteboard, Power Automate, Mixed Reality Portal, 3D Viewer, To Do, Quick Assist) - package identity and usage notes live in the function, not in a wildcard sweep. Apply emits the plan only; a removal requires a non-empty selection of catalog names plus -Approved. The shared engine refuses protected names (NX12-002), refuses a package with installed dependents outside the selection (NX12-014 graph), removes dependents before dependencies, refuses dependency cycles, and journals the exact PackageFullName/PackageFamilyName/version/architecture/scope/provisioned state before calling Remove-AppxPackage. A missing package is a skip, not an error. Maps is app-level only: NX11-016 still owns Maps service configuration. Widgets/taskbar is NX15 policy territory and the Widgets package is deliberately not in this catalog. Result label is 'Success-Irreversible'; the documented restore route is NX12-011. Re-running is idempotent (absent package -> Skipped-NotFound).
tweaks.defaultState: Windows ships the consumer apps; no NEXTRIX app changes.
tweaks.proposedState: Only owner-selected consumer apps removed for the selected scope; all other packages untouched.

verify.procedure: Plan lists the catalog with installed/provisioned/protected/dependent state; after a selected removal, Get-AppxPackage -Name returns nothing for the selected scope and the journal carries a verify entry labeled Success-Irreversible.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible: the package payload is not stored by NEXTRIX. Use NX12-011 (Microsoft Store/library or winget msstore with a verified ProductId) and re-check NX12-010; app data removed with the package is not restored.

originalState.method: Invoke-Nx12Removal journals package identity (name/full name/family/version/architecture/publisher/signature), scope, provisioned state, install location and declared dependencies before Remove-AppxPackage.

sideEffects: The selected app and its Start entry disappear for the chosen scope; app data may be removed with the package.
Other profiles are unaffected unless -Scope AllUsers is chosen (administrator required).
Microsoft documents that provisioned inbox apps can be re-applied by Windows feature updates, so a removed app may return after an upgrade; the ledger reports it.
Reinstalling requires Microsoft Store/App Installer, which NX12-002 protects and never removes.
No performance improvement is claimed or measured.
documentationSource: research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (WebView2 15+ app dependency; per-app removal discipline)

tweaks.name: Protected-dependency guard
tweaks.description: Defines and enforces the protected-by-default package list; reports findings and refuses protected removals from every engine path.
tweaks.objective: Make Store/App Installer/WebView2/runtime/OS-component removal impossible by default, and prove the refusal instead of trusting callers.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxProtectedDependencyReport (read-only) and the shared Test-Nx12PackageProtected guard used by Invoke-Nx12Removal, Invoke-Nx12ProvisionedRemoval and Invoke-Nx12CapabilityRemoval. Protection is three-layered: (1) exact identities - Microsoft.WindowsStore, Microsoft.StorePurchaseApp, Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller, Microsoft.Win32WebViewHost, Microsoft.MicrosoftEdge.Stable, Microsoft.Services.Store.Engagement, Microsoft.Windows.ShellExperienceHost, Microsoft.Windows.StartMenuExperienceHost, Microsoft.AAD.BrokerPlugin, Microsoft.AccountsControl, Microsoft.Windows.CloudExperienceHost, Microsoft.Windows.PeopleExperienceHost, Microsoft.Windows.SecHealthUI, Microsoft.Windows.Apprep.ChxApp, Microsoft.Windows.SecureAssessmentBrowser, Microsoft.Windows.Search, Microsoft.XboxIdentityProvider, Microsoft.GamingServices, Microsoft.GamingServicesNet, Microsoft.XboxGameCallableUI; (2) versioned patterns - Microsoft.VCLibs.*, Microsoft.NET.Native.*, Microsoft.UI.Xaml*, Microsoft.WindowsAppRuntime*, *WebView2*, MicrosoftWindows.Client.*; (3) the OS-component rule - any package whose SignatureKind is 'System' is protected even if it is not listed. The report also states the WebView2 distinction honestly: the Evergreen WebView2 Runtime is a Win32 component installed outside AppX, so AppX removal commands never touch it, while the WebView2 host packages are protected. Evidence: research records 15+ apps depending on WebView2 (r4), ReviOS re-provisioning VCLibs to fix a wsappx loop (r2), and Xbox-coupled removal fallout (ms-gamebar, r1). The guard returns a decision object (protected/ruleId/category/reason) and never throws, so every removal entry reports a refusal instead of failing open.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX protection report; unprotected removal scripts can remove these packages.
tweaks.proposedState: Protection report present and every removal path refuses protected identities before journaling.

verify.procedure: Report returns readOnly=true with rules, findings and guard probes; Microsoft.WindowsStore, Microsoft.DesktopAppInstaller, Microsoft.VCLibs.140.00 and Microsoft.Win32WebViewHost probe as protected while a consumer app such as Microsoft.BingNews probes as unprotected.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only report and an in-memory guard; nothing is modified.

sideEffects: Protected packages cannot be selected for removal by any NX12 entry; this is intentional and not user-overridable in v1.
System-signed packages are protected by rule, so a future catalog mistake cannot turn an OS component into a removal target.

tweaks.name: OEM/promotional third-party app removal
tweaks.description: Nominates preinstalled non-Microsoft promotional AppX packages and removes only individually consented ones.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a per-app way to drop OEM/promotional preinstalls without sweeping user-installed software.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family Oem (read-only nomination) and Remove-NxOemPromotionalApp (write path). A package is nominated only when its publisher is not Microsoft, its name is not Microsoft.*, it is not a framework, it is not protected by NX12-002, and either it is provisioned (OEM preinstall) or its name matches a known promotional title fragment. Anything owned by another NX12 catalog (consumer/comms/Xbox/Copilot/Phone Link) is excluded to prevent overlapping ownership. User-installed packages require the explicit -IncludeUserInstalled switch before they can even appear. Removal requires exact package names/family names plus -Approved -Approval ExplicitConsent; there is no 'remove all OEM apps' mode. Win32 OEM software (Programs and Features uninstallers) is out of scope and is not touched. Detection is a nomination heuristic, not a Microsoft-documented classification: the documented part is the AppX removal mechanism, while the candidate rule is NEXTRIX logic and is reported as such. Journal-first identity/scope/provisioned-state capture and Success-Irreversible labeling are inherited from the shared engine.
tweaks.defaultState: OEM/promotional AppX packages present as shipped.
tweaks.proposedState: Only individually consented promotional AppX packages removed; unrelated third-party apps untouched.

verify.procedure: Plan lists nominated candidates with publisher/provisioned/promo reason; after removal the selected package is absent for the chosen scope and a Success-Irreversible verify entry exists.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible; reinstall through the vendor/Store route documented by NX12-011 where the app is Store-distributed. OEM Win32 software is outside this entry's scope.

originalState.method: Shared engine journals identity, scope, provisioned state, publisher and signature before removal.

sideEffects: The vendor app and its integrations (e.g. trial security suites) disappear for the selected scope.
A vendor license/trial is not restored by reinstallation; vendor terms are the owner's responsibility.
Only AppX packages are in scope; Win32 OEM software remains in Programs and Features.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (Atlas gates app removals behind explicit choices)

tweaks.name: Phone Link removal (optional)
tweaks.description: Removes the Phone Link app (Microsoft.YourPhone) on explicit selection; declared symmetric conflict with NX13-012.
tweaks.objective: Remove the phone-linking client without touching shared cross-device platform services.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxPhoneLinkState; the apply action is the read-only Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family PhoneLink. Only Microsoft.YourPhone is targeted. The Cross Device Service host (MicrosoftWindows.CrossDevice) is deliberately NOT removed: it also serves other cross-device features and is platform plumbing. The documented phone-PC linking policy (EnableMmx / AllowPhonePCLinking) belongs to NX13-012, which declares NX12-004 symmetrically; removing the app and disabling the policy attack the same feature, so the function reports whether the policy is already set and the entry tells the owner to choose one. Removal is per-user by default, requires -Approved, and inherits the protected guard, dependency graph and journal-first identity/scope/provisioned-state capture. Microsoft documents that the app can be reinstalled from the Store; the result is labeled Success-Irreversible for journal purposes and can return after a feature update. No service is reconfigured (NX11 owns services).
tweaks.proposedState: Microsoft.YourPhone absent for the selected scope; cross-device platform host and policies unchanged.

verify.procedure: Plan shows Microsoft.YourPhone present/absent and protected=false; after removal Get-AppxPackage -Name Microsoft.YourPhone returns nothing for the selected scope and the journal entry is labeled Success-Irreversible.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible; reinstall Phone Link from Microsoft Store (NX12-011). Previously linked phones must be re-linked after reinstall.

originalState.method: Shared engine journals package identity, scope and provisioned state before removal; the function also reports the NX13-012 policy state read-only.

sideEffects: Phone Link, its Start entry and phone-screen/messaging integration disappear for the selected profile.
Continue on PC / phone linking stops for that profile; NX13-012 policy is the alternative control for the same feature.
Cross-device clipboard and other Cross Device Service features are NOT changed by this entry.
The app can return after a Windows feature update or be reinstalled from the Store.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (Revi YourPhone removal and its revert ledger)

tweaks.name: Xbox app removal (optional)
tweaks.description: Removes the Xbox app (Microsoft.GamingApp) and optionally the legacy Xbox Console Companion; Game Pass users are excluded by evidence gate.
tweaks.objective: Remove the Xbox client UI for owners who do not use Game Pass, without touching gaming platform dependencies.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxXboxAppState; the apply action is Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family Xbox. Only Microsoft.GamingApp and the legacy Microsoft.XboxApp are removable. Microsoft.XboxIdentityProvider, Microsoft.GamingServices, Microsoft.GamingServicesNet, Microsoft.XboxGameCallableUI and Game Bar are protected by NX12-002 and are never targets: research records Gaming Services as required for Game Pass install/update/play (r2, NX02-008, NX11-010), and Xbox service sweeps breaking XboxGipSvc. Game Pass exclusion: strong evidence (installed Xbox/Game Pass game folders under the system drive's XboxGames directory) refuses the removal outright; Gaming Services/service presence is reported as weak evidence only because it ships broadly and is not proof of a subscription. Removing the Xbox app while Game Bar remains can produce the documented ms-gamebar controller popup (r1), so the write function requires -AcknowledgeGameBarRisk after reading that note. Declared symmetric conflicts: NX02-008 and NX11-010; the result reports both. No service, task or registry gaming value is changed here.
tweaks.defaultState: Xbox app installed as shipped; gaming services untouched.
tweaks.proposedState: Xbox client app absent for the selected scope; identity provider, Gaming Services and Game Bar intact.

verify.procedure: Plan reports Game Pass evidence and candidate state; removal refuses when strong Game Pass evidence exists or the Game Bar acknowledgement is missing; after an approved removal the selected package is absent and the journal entry is Success-Irreversible.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible; reinstall the Xbox app from Microsoft Store (NX12-011). Services were never changed, so no service rollback is required.

originalState.method: Shared engine journals identity, scope and provisioned state before removal; the function records Game Pass evidence and the acknowledgement in its result.

sideEffects: The Xbox app UI, its game-library entry point and achievements/social surfaces disappear for the selected scope.
Game Pass installs are excluded by the evidence gate; if evidence is incomplete, the owner must verify manually before selecting this entry.
Game Bar/capture remains installed; the documented ms-gamebar popup can appear for controller use after Xbox app removal (r1).
Gaming Services, identity provider and services are untouched; service background activity is NX11's territory.
The app can return after a feature update or be reinstalled from the Store.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (XboxGipSvc/Xbox service dependency ledger; Game Pass dependency)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX12-005 (conflict NX02-008; Game Pass users excluded)
Catalogue XREF: NX11-010 Xbox services configuration (symmetric conflict)

tweaks.name: Copilot / AI feature configuration
tweaks.description: Removes the Microsoft.Copilot app with Microsoft's documented uninstall procedure, gated on build and package presence.
tweaks.objective: Disable the consumer Copilot app experience without writing a deprecated policy or guessing at build-specific surfaces.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxCopilotState; the apply action is Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family Copilot (read-only). Microsoft's 'Manage Windows Copilot' documentation gives the exact uninstall procedure (Get-AppxPackage -Name Microsoft.Copilot then Remove-AppxPackage) and states that TurnOffWindowsCopilot is a legacy policy 'subject to near-term deprecation', recommending AppLocker instead. NEXTRIX therefore removes the AppX through the documented procedure, does NOT write the deprecated policy, and does NOT manage AppLocker. Availability is build/region/update dependent: the function checks the build against ADR-003 and reports Skipped-NotFound when the package is absent instead of pretending success. Per-user scope is the default; AllUsers requires elevation. Research records reference projects disabling Copilot through policies and one attempting winget-based removal as an undocumented mechanism (r5) - the latter is rejected; this entry uses only the Microsoft-documented AppX route. Because applicability is conditional and the AI surface changes quickly, evidence is E0 even though the removal mechanism itself is documented. Label: Success-Irreversible; reinstall route: Store/Windows updates (NX12-011), not guaranteed.
tweaks.defaultState: Copilot app present where the build/region provides it and no policy blocks it.
tweaks.proposedState: Microsoft.Copilot absent for the selected scope; deprecated policy untouched.

verify.procedure: Function reports build scope and package presence; absent package -> Skipped-NotFound; after removal Get-AppxPackage -Name Microsoft.Copilot returns nothing and the journal verify entry is Success-Irreversible.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible; reinstall through Microsoft Store/Windows updates if the app is offered for this build/region (NX12-011). The deprecated policy was never written, so there is no policy to remove.

originalState.method: Shared engine journals identity, scope and provisioned state before removal; the function journals the build/presence decision in its result.

sideEffects: The Copilot app and its app-level entry points disappear for the selected profile.
The Copilot hardware key / Win+C may still open a web-based experience depending on build; this entry does not remap keys.
Future Windows updates may reinstall or re-surface Copilot; the ledger reports a return.
No deprecated policy is written; administrators who need policy-level control are pointed to Microsoft's documented AppLocker guidance, which NEXTRIX does not manage.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/client-management/manage-windows-copilot (documented Get-AppxPackage/Remove-AppxPackage procedure; TurnOffWindowsCopilot legacy/deprecation note; AppLocker guidance)
research/sources/r5-winutil-sophia.md (winget Copilot removal as undocumented/fragile - rejected)

tweaks.name: Communication apps optional removal
tweaks.description: Removes selected communication apps (Skype, Mail and Calendar, People, new Outlook, Teams) with per-app consent and dependency checks.
tweaks.objective: Let the owner drop unused communication clients without breaking contact stores, work/school Teams or other apps by accident.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxCommunicationAppState; the apply action is Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family Communications. The catalog is explicit: Microsoft.SkypeApp, Microsoft.WindowsCommunicationsApps (Mail and Calendar), Microsoft.People, Microsoft.OutlookForWindows, MSTeams and the legacy MicrosoftTeams identity. Each row carries a usage note; MSTeams is the unified personal AND work/school client and requires -AcknowledgeTeamsWorkload because removal breaks work/school sign-in. People is the contact-store UI used by Mail/Calendar surfaces and is flagged accordingly. The shared engine checks the dependency graph first (NX12-014), refuses packages with installed dependents outside the selection, and journals identity/scope/provisioned state before removal. Empty selections return the read-only plan; unknown names are refused. Label Success-Irreversible; reinstall through the Store (NX12-011). No service or protocol handler is modified.
tweaks.proposedState: Only selected communication apps removed for the selected scope.

verify.procedure: Plan shows each communication app with present/protected/dependent state and the Teams acknowledgement requirement; after removal the selected package is absent for the scope and journaled Success-Irreversible.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible; reinstall from Microsoft Store (NX12-011). Teams work/school data remains server-side; local app data is not restored.

originalState.method: Shared engine journals identity, scope and provisioned state before removal; the Teams acknowledgement is recorded in the result.

sideEffects: Selected clients and their Start entries disappear; mail/calendar/contact integrations may lose their in-box UI.
Removing People affects contact management surfaces used by Mail/Calendar.
Removing Teams breaks personal and work/school sign-in for that client until reinstalled.
Alternative clients are unaffected; no protocol handler is changed.
Apps can return after feature updates or be reinstalled from the Store.

tweaks.name: Removal scope control (per-user / all-users)
tweaks.description: Reports and documents the per-user, all-users and provisioned removal scopes with live record counts before any removal.
tweaks.objective: Make the blast radius of a removal explicit and journal it per scope, so a profile-level removal is never mistaken for a machine-wide one.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxRemovalScopeReport (read-only). Microsoft documents the Remove-AppxPackage -AllUsers parameter as removing for all user accounts (administrator required) and -User as restricting removal to one user SID; Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage affects only new profiles. The report returns, per package: current-user installed (boolean), all-users record count, provisioned state and the three scope descriptions. It deliberately returns counts and booleans only - no SIDs, user names or profile paths - so the report is privacy-safe and can sit in a support bundle. The shared engine records original.scope on every removal entry, which is what NX12-010 and the rollback report use to distinguish CurrentUser from AllUsers from Provisioned. AllUsers requires elevation; the engine refuses it otherwise. This entry itself mutates nothing.
tweaks.defaultState: No scope report; removal scope is implicit in a command line.
tweaks.proposedState: Explicit scope report and per-removal journaled scope.

verify.procedure: Report returns readOnly=true, per-package current/all-users/provisioned rows and the three scope descriptions; allUsersAvailable reflects whether the elevated query succeeded.

originalState.method: Not applicable - read-only; the engine journals scope at removal time.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
On a non-elevated session the all-users count is reported as unavailable rather than guessed.

tweaks.name: Provisioned package removal control
tweaks.description: Removes exact provisioned packages with explicit consent, journaling identity and provisioned state; existing user installs are untouched.
tweaks.objective: Control what new user profiles receive without altering existing profiles' installed apps.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Remove-NxProvisionedPackageControl and the shared Invoke-Nx12ProvisionedRemoval engine; the apply action is Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family Provisioned. Microsoft documents Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage precisely: it removes app packages from a Windows image so they 'will not be installed when new user accounts are created', and 'packages will not be removed from existing user accounts'. The entry therefore states that distinction in its result and side effects instead of implying a machine-wide uninstall. Selection is exact provisioned PackageName identities (no wildcard sweep), -Approved and -Approval ExplicitConsent are mandatory, elevation is required, and the protected guard applies to the package base name. If the DISM provisioning subsystem cannot be read, nothing is removed and the result is Unverified - never a guessed success. Re-provisioning requires the original package payload/image, so the label is MediaRequired / Success-Irreversible. A subsequent feature update may re-provision packages; the ledger reports the state.
tweaks.defaultState: Provisioned packages present in the image; new profiles receive them.
tweaks.proposedState: Selected provisioned packages absent; new profiles do not receive them; existing profiles unchanged.

verify.procedure: Plan lists provisioned identities with protected flags; after removal Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online no longer lists the selected PackageName and the journal verify entry is Success-Irreversible; an unreadable provisioning list yields Unverified with no mutation.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible: re-provisioning requires the original app package/image payload. NX12-011 documents the route and the ledger labels it MediaRequired.

originalState.method: Journals the provisioned PackageName, display name, base name, version, architecture, install location, scope=Provisioned and provisioned state before removal.

sideEffects: New user profiles will not receive the removed package; existing profiles keep it (Microsoft-documented).
Some inbox apps may be re-provisioned by a Windows feature update; the ledger reports a return.
Reinstalling for a specific user is possible through the Store, but re-provisioning for future users needs the original payload.

tweaks.name: Removal history & reversibility ledger
tweaks.description: Read-only ledger of every NX12 AppX/provisioned/capability removal with an honest Store-reinstallable vs media-requiring label and live presence check.
tweaks.objective: One truthful place to see what was removed, whether it came back, and exactly what restoration would require.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxRemovalLedger. It reads the state journal through Read-NxJournal, so the integrity chain is verified first; any integrity error aborts the ledger instead of presenting a tampered history as fact. Entries with targetType appx/appxProvisioned/capability are grouped by target+package+scope, newest sequence wins, and each row reports: scope, provisioned state, last operation/result/verification, reversibility label (StoreReinstallable / MediaRequired / OptionalFeature), reinstall route, history count, and a live presence check for AppX packages. Status is Removed, ReturnedOrReinstalled (journal says removed but the package is present now - the documented feature-update return behavior or a user/Store reinstall), RemovalIncomplete (last operation failed), or Unknown. No SIDs or profile identifiers are emitted. The ledger never restores anything: restoration is NX12-011. This is the honesty surface for the directive requirement that AppX removals are not disguised as reversible.
tweaks.defaultState: Journal entries exist but no consolidated ledger view.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only ledger with labels, live status and reinstall routes.

verify.procedure: Ledger returns readOnly=true, per-item labels/status/reinstall routes and counts; with an empty journal it returns zero items without error; with an integrity error it sets aborted=true and lists the errors.

originalState.method: Not applicable - reads journaled originals; never writes package state.

sideEffects: None (read-only).
A package reinstalled outside NEXTRIX is reported as ReturnedOrReinstalled, not silently treated as still removed.
documentationSource: ROLLBACK_DESIGN.md (AppX row: identity/scope/provisioned state + honest label)
research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (removed apps return after updates; official uninstall limits)

tweaks.name: Reinstallation helper (Store-based)
tweaks.description: Separate documented restoration path: reports Store/library and winget-msstore routes, and installs only with an explicit verified ProductId.
tweaks.objective: Give AppX removals a real, documented recovery path without pretending the journal can replay package payloads.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Restore-NxRemovedApp. Default -Mode Report is read-only: it reads the NX12-010 ledger, lists each removed item with the Microsoft Store > Library route and the exact 'winget search <name> --source msstore' command, and never contacts the network. -Mode Install requires -Approved, exactly one package name and a verified -ProductId; NEXTRIX does not guess Microsoft Store product ids (an undocumented winget Copilot removal is explicitly rejected in research, r5). The install call uses the documented msstore source with accepted source/package agreements, then verifies presence through Get-AppxPackage. Reinstall attempts are journaled as 'verify' entries (ReinstallRequested / Reinstalled / ReinstallFailed), never as 'apply', so rollback can never mistake a reinstall for a removal. App data removed with the package is not restored; sign-in may be required. App Installer/winget is protected by NX12-002, so this path cannot be broken by NEXTRIX's own debloating.
tweaks.defaultState: No helper; removed apps require manual Store navigation.
tweaks.proposedState: Read-only restore plan and an auditable, explicit install path.

verify.procedure: Report mode lists removed items with Store/library and winget-search routes and is read-only; Install mode requires ProductId, journals verify entries, and reports Reinstalled only when Get-AppxPackage sees the package again.

rollback.procedure: The reinstall is additive; undoing it means removing the app again through the matching NX12 removal entry (itself irreversible). The helper never claims to restore app data.

originalState.method: Reads the journaled removal identity; Install mode journals the requested product id and verification result as verify entries.

sideEffects: Install mode uses the network and Microsoft Store/App Installer; a download and sign-in may be required.
App data deleted with the package is not restored.
A Store app may be unavailable in the current region or renamed; the helper reports the search route rather than inventing an id.
A reinstalled inbox app is a normal Store app again; feature-update behavior is unchanged.
documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (Store reinstall flakiness; manual reinstall required)
research/sources/r5-winutil-sophia.md (winget Copilot removal undocumented/fragile - ids are not guessed)

tweaks.name: Windows capabilities selective removal
tweaks.description: Removes only individually selected capabilities from a documented allow-list that carries usage notes and reinstall routes; never a blanket removal.
tweaks.objective: Allow optional feature removal while protecting language packs, biometrics, frameworks and shell components.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxOptionalCapabilityInventory (read-only) and Remove-NxOptionalCapability in src/nxcore/functions/NX12.ps1. The allow-list contains MathRecognizer, Media.WindowsMediaPlayer, Microsoft.Windows.PowerShell.ISE, Microsoft.Windows.WordPad, OpenSSH.Client, Print.Management.Console, StepsRecorder, VBSCRIPT, WMIC, Browser.InternetExplorer, App.Support.QuickAssist, App.WirelessDisplay.Connect, XPS.Viewer and Rsat.* (prefix), each with a usage note and reinstall command. Anything else is refused, and a protected pattern layer (Language.*, Hello.*, NetFX.*, Microsoft.Windows.Notepad/Paint/Shell/Client/Photos*, OpenSSH.Server*) refuses even if a future edit tried to allow it. Removal requires exact capability names, -Approved and -Approval ExplicitConsent, elevation, and journals the capability name/state before Remove-WindowsCapability; verification re-reads State=NotPresent. If DISM is unavailable, the inventory reports uncertainty and removal refuses/returns Unverified rather than guessing. Reinstallation is Settings > Optional features or Add-WindowsCapability, which may require Windows Update or media, so the honest label is OptionalFeature / Success-Irreversible.
tweaks.defaultState: Optional capabilities present as shipped by the build.
tweaks.proposedState: Only selected allow-listed capabilities removed; protected/other capabilities untouched.

verify.procedure: Inventory returns the allow-list with state/usage/reinstall routes; after removal Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name <name> reports NotPresent and the journal verify entry is Success-Irreversible; unreadable DISM yields Unverified.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible; reinstall through Settings > Optional features or Add-WindowsCapability -Online (Windows Update or media source may be required). NX12-011 reports the route.

originalState.method: Journals capability name, display name, state, scope=Machine and reversibility=OptionalFeature before removal.

sideEffects: The selected capability's feature disappears until reinstalled.
Reinstall may need Windows Update access or installation media; an offline machine may not be able to restore it immediately.
Language packs, Hello biometrics, .NET, Notepad/Paint and shell components are hard-refused and unaffected.
documentationSource: research/sources/r2-atlasos-revios.md (optional component removal as an explicit choice)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX12-012 (never blanket; per-capability usage notes)

tweaks.name: New-user app provisioning policy
tweaks.description: Deprovisions selected consumer app families so new Windows profiles do not receive them, with per-family explicit consent.
tweaks.objective: Make a lasting new-user policy decision instead of re-removing apps in every profile.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Set-NxNewUserProvisioningPolicy; the apply action is Get-Nx12RemovalPlan -Family ProvisioningPolicy. Families are explicit consumer groups (News & Weather, Consumer games, Consumer media, Consumer productivity, Support & feedback apps, Mixed Reality & 3D), and each maps to a fixed package list. Only provisioned packages are touched, through the same Invoke-Nx12ProvisionedRemoval engine as NX12-009: exact PackageName identities, protected guard, journal-first provisioned state, -Approved plus -Approval ExplicitConsent, elevation. Microsoft documents that Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage prevents installation for NEW user accounts and does not remove packages from existing accounts, so this entry never claims a machine-wide uninstall. App families owned by NX12-004/005/006/007 are deliberately absent to avoid cross-entry ownership; a second run for the same package reports Skipped-NotFound/Already absent. Re-provisioning needs the original payload (MediaRequired) and a feature update may re-provision; the ledger reports it.
tweaks.defaultState: Provisioned consumer packages installed for new profiles.
tweaks.proposedState: Selected consumer families deprovisioned; new profiles do not receive them; existing profiles unchanged.

verify.procedure: Plan lists families with per-package provisioned/installed/protected state; after deprovisioning the selected PackageName is absent from Get-AppxProvisionedPackage and the verify entry is Success-Irreversible; existing profile installs are reported unchanged.

rollback.procedure: Not journal-reversible: re-provisioning needs the original package payload/image. NX12-011 and NX12-010 document the route and label it MediaRequired.

originalState.method: Journals each provisioned PackageName, family, version, architecture, install location and provisioned state before removal.

sideEffects: New profiles created after apply will not receive the selected apps; existing profiles keep their installs.
A feature update may re-provision inbox apps, which the ledger reports.
Removing provisioning does not remove the app from the current user; combine with NX12-001 only if that is intended.

tweaks.name: AppX dependency graph verification engine
tweaks.description: Builds the installed-package dependency graph and verifies that a removal has no installed dependents; the tooling gate for every NX12 removal.
tweaks.objective: Prevent a removal that silently breaks another app or runtime, and refuse instead of guessing when the graph cannot be proven.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Implemented by Get-NxAppxDependencyGraph (read-only) plus the shared Sort-Nx12RemovalOrder/Test guards used by Invoke-Nx12Removal and Invoke-Nx12ProvisionedRemoval. Nodes are installed AppX packages (deduplicated by name) with their declared Appx dependencies; edges point from a dependency family to its dependents. For a focus package the report returns direct and transitive dependents, protected status and a safeToRemove verdict. The graph also reports anomalies where a declared dependency family is not installed, and never guesses a failed read (uncertainty list). The removal engine uses it twice: it orders a selection dependents-first (topological order) and refuses any package whose installed dependents are outside the selection, re-checking live after earlier removals; dependency cycles are refused rather than blindly ordered. Protected runtimes (VCLibs, .NET Native, UI.Xaml, Windows App Runtime, WebView2) are both protected and graph hubs, so they are doubly unreachable. Provisioned-only packages are not graph nodes unless the DISM query succeeds; that limitation is reported.
tweaks.defaultState: No dependency evidence; removals can break dependents.
tweaks.proposedState: Dependency graph report available and enforced by every removal path.

verify.procedure: Report returns readOnly=true with node/edge counts, protected node count, anomalies and focus verdicts; a protected focus package reports safeToRemove=false, and an installed dependent blocks its dependency.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; the engine's only effect is refusing or ordering removals.

originalState.method: Not applicable - read-only package metadata query.

sideEffects: None when used as a report.
The graph depends on Appx package metadata; unreadable metadata is reported as uncertainty, and a removal path refuses rather than assuming there are no dependents.
